name: Deathstep - Wavetable FM screech
description: Reference checklist for a high screech lead on Ableton Wavetable: FM oscillator effect tuned an octave or two up, a 24 dB low-pass around 200 Hz with modest resonance, a hard filter envelope, a resonant high-pass and a short delay. Not executable: the engine cannot create Wavetable patches on Live 12.2.5.

manual.instruction: In Wavetable's oscillator effects, choose FM, set the tune to 100% (the modulator goes two octaves up) and bring the amount up to roughly 25-35%. Start from a plain table so the FM is the sound.
manual.verify: A bright, glassy tone with a clear sideband character rather than a plain saw.
manual.why: Attack Magazine's Wavetable foghorn patch uses exactly these FM tune and amount values as its starting point.

manual.instruction: Set the filter to a 24 dB low-pass, cutoff near 200 Hz and resonance around 25%. Shape Env 2 to open quickly and close slowly so the screech has a bite and then a tail.
manual.verify: The attack is sharp and the note settles into a narrower tone.
manual.why: The same patch uses a 24 dB filter near 200 Hz and about 25% resonance, with an envelope that opens then closes.

manual.instruction: Turn the pitch envelope on and give it a downward move of several semitones over a short decay. A screech that sits still reads as a synth note; a falling one reads as a scream.
manual.verify: The note bends down at the front without losing its pitch centre.
manual.why: Pitch drops are the standard way to turn a bright tone into a screech or siren in this family of styles.

manual.instruction: Add a resonant high-pass after the synth, around 500-800 Hz, and sweep it only on transitions. Then push Redux or Erosion lightly for aliasing grit.
manual.verify: The screech cuts through a full drop without being boosted in level.
manual.why: A thin, bright layer sits above the bass instead of competing with it for the same band.

manual.instruction: Add a short tempo-synced delay at 1/8 with the feedback low and the filter high, so the screech answers itself between the main hits.
manual.verify: The delay is audible as an answer, not as wash.
manual.why: Short delays on a high layer are how these styles imply a second voice without writing another part.

manual.instruction: Resample the screech once it works, then pitch and chop the audio for the second drop. Keep one instance of the live patch for edits.
manual.verify: The second drop has a variant of the sound without a second synth instance.
manual.why: Resampling is the standard way to build variants while keeping CPU and tuning under control.

notes: Sources: Attack Magazine's Wavetable foghorn tutorial for the FM/filter/envelope values (https://www.attackmagazine.com/technique/synth-secrets/drum-n-bass-foghorn-bass-with-wavetable); Melodigging's deathstep notes for the genre use of FM and wavetable sources (https://www.melodigging.com/genre/deathstep). The high-pass and delay steps are standard practice applied to the genre, not transcript quotes. Reference-only.
